On physical examination, his blood pressure is 160/90 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm, respiratory rate is 22 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral rales halfway up both lung fields.
Cardiac examination shows a laterally displaced apical impulse and a holosystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla.
Extremities are notable for 2+ pitting edema up to the mid-shins.
Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion.
An echocardiogram reveals left ventricular hypertrophy, dilated left ventricle with an ejection fraction of 30%, and mitral valve leaflets with normal structure.

encounters.cc: Diabetic foot ulcer with fever, tachycardia, and ventricular tachycardia on telemetry.

lines: Diabetic foot ulcer with fever, tachycardia, and ventricular tachycardia on telemetry.
The patient is a 71-year-old male with diabetes, heart failure, and multiple myeloma, hospitalized six months prior for heart failure, who is admitted for management of a diabetic foot ulcer.
On hospital day 2, the patient develops a fever of 38.5°C, tachycardia with a heart rate of 110 bpm, and a blood pressure of 135/85 mmHg.
Over the next 24 hours, the telemetry monitor alarms frequently for ventricular tachycardia.
